white_space: No single competitor bridges existing fridge/pantry inventory tracking with weekly dinner planning and an automated shopping list: inventory trackers like C:PantryGenie and recipe improvisers like C:FridgeChef do not build weekly plans, while weekly planners like C:MealLoop, C:PlanPlate, C:WeekWise, and C:SupperSync do not track household inventory.
No competitor offers automated deduction of on-hand inventory when generating grocery lists for a household weekly meal plan (C:MealLoop, C:PantryGenie, C:SupperSync).
pricing_anchors: Competitor subscription prices range from EUR 2.99/month (C:PlanPlate) to EUR 6.99/month (C:MealLoop, or approx. EUR 4.17/month on its EUR 49.99/year plan), with median stated consumer willingness to pay for cooking apps sitting at EUR 3.50 per month (S05). Direct household tools charge EUR 3.99/month (C:PantryGenie) and EUR 4.49/month per household (C:SupperSync), making EUR 3.50 to EUR 4.49/month the realistic pricing corridor; any price above EUR 6.99/month is untested and unsupported.

idea_claim_checks.claim: Existing recipe apps give ideas but do not know what you already own.
idea_claim_checks.explanation: Competitor evidence directly contradicts this blanket statement. C:FridgeChef suggests recipes from photos of fridge contents, C:PantryGenie tracks barcode pantry inventory, and C:ZeroWaste Kitchen provides use-it-up recipes for leftover ingredients. True differentiation lies not in inventory awareness alone, but in combining inventory awareness with structured weekly dinner planning.
